description:
Roboticados EPM es un club de formación en robótica dirigido principalmente a niños y jóvenes interesados en la tecnología, la programación, la electrónica, el diseño y la construcción de sistemas robóticos.

El club nació en 2022 como un semillero de robótica y, a través de un proceso de formación continua, ha evolucionado hacia un espacio donde los participantes desarrollan proyectos, fortalecen sus conocimientos técnicos y ponen a prueba sus habilidades en competencias y eventos de robótica.
summary:
AstroHealth AI is a health monitoring console for astronauts on long-duration missions. It gathers vital signs (BPM, SpO2, sleep, reaction time, fatigue) plus optional metrics (blood glucose, blood pressure, body temperature, mood, radiation, cabin CO2), evaluates them against clinical thresholds, and surfaces the five NASA spaceflight hazards: radiation, isolation and confinement, altered gravity, hostile environment, and distance. A fully local AI companion (Ollama, no cloud) turns the numbers into plain-language guidance and emotional support, so the crew can evaluate and act on their health autonomously, millions of kilometers from Earth.

AstroHealth AI is a tablet-style mission console with four screens:
HOME — mission dashboard with live health status (green / yellow / red) and AI advice.
DATA — the five NASA hazards with pre-flight / in-flight / post-flight comparisons (NASA LSDA & OSDR datasets), plus a manual sensor & log entry form. Required metrics: BPM, SpO2, sleep hours, reaction time (PVT), fatigue level. Optional: blood glucose, blood pressure, body temperature, mood, radiation dose, cabin CO2, cabin temperature, weight, notes.
AI—a local LLM companion ("AstroAI", built on Ollama) that analyzes the latest metrics and answers in plain language, with an emotional-support persona for isolation and confinement. Works fully offline; no data leaves the spacecraft.
PROFILE — astronaut profile with photo upload, XP score, logging streak, and crew gamification ranking.
details: AstroHealth AI lets a Mars-class crew gather, evaluate and act on their health autonomously, with no real-time ground support. The crew logs required metrics (BPM, SpO2, sleep hours, reaction time/PVT, fatigue) plus optional ones (blood glucose, blood pressure, body temperature, mood, radiation dose, cabin CO2) in a tablet-style console. A rule-based engine classifies every metric against documented clinical thresholds (normal/attention/bad/critical) and computes the status of the five NASA spaceflight hazards — radiation, isolation and confinement, altered gravity, hostile environment, and distance — each documented with the metrics that feed it. A fully local AI companion (a custom Ollama model, no cloud) turns the numbers into plain-language guidance and emotional support for isolation, with a rule-based fallback if the model is unavailable. Gamification (XP, streaks, crew ranking, bonuses for healthy habits) nudges astronauts toward consistent self-monitoring. Benefits: early risk detection, autonomous decision support, and behavioral health care millions of kilometers from Earth. Tools: Python, FastAPI, SQLite, vanilla HTML/JS/CSS, Chart.js, Ollama (llama3.2:3b with a custom health/emotional-support Modelfile). We used NASA LSDA and OSDR public data to shape the 32 metric datasets and the hazard model. The project is creative in combining rule-based clinical thresholds, a local LLM companion, and gamification into one offline-first console designed for crew autonomy. We considered offline operation, honest failure states (the UI never fakes healthy data when the backend is down), and judge reproducibility (one-command setup scripts).
